posts.subject: Yoga Pro 27UD-10 built-in speaker issues
posts.author: EnDelt
posts.message_html:
I purchased the Yoga Pro 27UD-10 monitor a few days ago. Overall, I’m very satisfied with it, but I believe there may be some bugs related to the built-in speakers, so I’d like to report the following issues.

  1. In Windows 11, if I enable the “Turn off my screen after” setting, there are times when the audio stops working after the display turns off and then wakes up again. The volume level and Windows sound settings still appear to be normal.
  2. When I connect my M2 MacBook Pro to the monitor via USB4 with Power Delivery, the audio sometimes suddenly becomes much louder or stops working entirely.

In both cases, the issue can be temporarily resolved by turning the monitor off and back on, or by disconnecting and reconnecting the monitor’s power cable. However, considering that this is a monitor that costs over $1,000, I believe these issues should definitely be addressed.

I’m not sure whether this is a hardware or software issue, but if it is software-related, I would appreciate it if Lenovo could provide a firmware or driver update to resolve it.

posts.subject: Re:Yoga Pro 27UD-10 built-in speaker issues
posts.author: Lorenzo_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello EnDelt,

Welcome to Lenovo Community

I understand that the built-in speakers of your Yoga Pro 27UD-10 monitor are having issues wherein it stops working or behave unpredictably after wake or over USB4.
Based on what you described, this may involve the monitor’s audio path resetting incorrectly after sleep/wake or when the USB4 connection reinitializes. Since the speakers recover after power-cycling the monitor, that suggests the monitor, connection handshake, or audio routing may need further investigation rather than this pointing only to a Windows volume setting.
Here are some steps you can try now:
1. In Windows 11, after the issue happens, go to Sound Settings and confirm the monitor is still selected as the active output device.

2. In Device Manager, remove the audio output entry associated with the monitor, then restart the computer so Windows reloads it.

3. Test with a different cable (Lenovo cables are highly recommended) if available, even if the current one appears to work for display and charging.

4. If the monitor has multiple input methods available, test another connection type temporarily to see whether the issue is limited to one path.

5. On the MacBook Pro, after the loudness jump or audio loss occurs, recheck Sound Output and test whether disconnecting and reconnecting only the USB4 cable changes the behavior before power-cycling the monitor.

6. If available in your setup, test the monitor with one device at a time to rule out switching-related behavior.

7. Check the monitor’s on-screen menu for any audio-related settings and make sure volume, mute, and input-related audio options remain stable after wake.

8. Ensure that your monitor's firmware and driver are up to date. See the support page for latest available updates.
Test, observe and let me know how things go. Besides the MacBook Pro, please indicate what computer are you using. If possible, kindly include the full MTM (machine type model), BIOS and OS build version.


Best regards,
Lorenzo_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Yoga Pro 27UD-10 built-in speaker issues
posts.author: EnDelt
posts.message_html:
1. The monitor is still correctly selected as the active audio output device when the issue occurs.
  2. The issue still occurs even after removing and reloading the audio output device entry.
  3. I have not been able to test this with a different cable. The monitor did not come with a Lenovo-branded cable. Also, the cable I am currently using has worked without any issues with other devices so far.
  4. It seems to work fine when connected via DisplayPort, but I cannot say this with certainty since I have not tested it continuously for several days.
  5. After the issue occurs, reconnecting the USB4 cable sometimes resolves the issue, but in other cases the issue occurs again.
  6. It seems to work fine when only one device is connected to the monitor at a time.
  7. The audio-related settings in the monitor’s on-screen menu remain unchanged after waking from sleep.
  8. The monitor firmware is already up to date. I am currently using firmware version V1.0.
